relationships.subject: H4K8 lactylation
relationships.evidence_quote: The schematic shows that pathological pain upregulates lactic acid in the DRG, leading to increased lactylation of histone H4K8, which inhibits Dock4 gene transcription

relationships.subject: DOCK4
relationships.evidence_quote: Importantly, TAM-induced conditionally knock-out of DOCK4 in DRG neurons significantly decreased thermal nociceptive threshold in mice (Fig. 3k–r), eliciting thermal hyperalgesia.

relationships.subject: DOCK4
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, DOCK4 interacts with sodium channel Nav1.7 and mediates its trafficking from the membrane to the cytoplasm in DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: DOCK4
relationships.evidence_quote: Acting an adaptor protein, DOCK4 binds the motor protein Dynein to form a Dynein/DOCK4/Nav1.7 complex, where Dynein provides the mechanical force for Nav1.7 trafficking.

relationships.subject: LDHA
relationships.evidence_quote: Injection of sodium oxamate (an LDH inhibitor)27 (Fig. 2i), which decreased lactate levels (Fig. S2d) and Pan Kla (Fig. S2e), significantly increased the expression of DOCK4 in the DRG tissues (Fig. 2j, k).

key_findings: DOCK4 is decreased in DRG across four pain models via H4K8 lactylation at its promoter; LDH inhibition by oxamate restores it.
DOCK4 loss in sensory neurons selectively increases heat nociception, via a Dynein/DOCK4/Nav1.7 trafficking complex.
